notes.summary: A cube (die) has 6 faces in 3 opposite pairs; every face touches the other 4. Dice questions ask which face is opposite another, using views of the die or its open net, which cube a net can make, and how many small cubes of a painted cube have paint on 0, 1, 2 or 3 faces.

concepts.title: Cube facts
concepts.body:
• 6 faces, 3 pairs of opposite faces. Each face is adjacent to 4 faces and opposite exactly 1.
  • One view of a die shows 3 faces that meet at a corner. They are all adjacent, so none of them is opposite another.
  • On a standard die, opposite faces add up to 7 (1–6, 2–5, 3–4). Use this only when the question says the die is standard.

concepts.title: Opposite face: elimination
concepts.body:
Collect every face seen together with the given face in any view. Those are adjacent. The one face never seen with it is its opposite.

Mini example: 1 appears with 2, 3 (view i) and with 4, 5 (view ii). The only face never seen with 1 is 6, so 6 is opposite 1.

concepts.title: Opposite face: common-face rules
concepts.body:
• One common face in the same position: the faces in matching positions are opposite.
  • One common face in different positions (clockwise method): in each view, read the three faces clockwise, starting from the common face. The second faces of the two lists are opposite, and so are the third faces.
  • Two common faces: the two remaining faces (one from each view) are opposite.

Reading clockwise in a drawn die: top, then the right-hand face, then the left-hand face. In the figure: view (i) gives 1, 3, 2 and view (ii) gives 1, 6, 5. So 3 is opposite 6 and 2 is opposite 5, which leaves 1 opposite 4.

concepts.title: Open nets: finding opposite faces
concepts.body:
• In a straight line of squares, skip one: the 1st and 3rd are opposite, as are the 2nd and 4th.
  • Squares that share an edge are adjacent, never opposite.
  • In a Z or staircase shape, the two squares at the ends of the Z are opposite.
  • A cube has 11 different nets; every one gives exactly 3 opposite pairs. Check that your three pairs use all six faces once.

In the figure: staircase net gives 1–4, 2–5, 3–6; the 3 + 3 net gives 1–3, 4–6, 2–5.

concepts.title: From a net to a cube
concepts.body:
1. Find the 3 opposite pairs from the net.
  2. Reject any cube that shows two opposite faces together.
  3. For the cubes left, fold mentally: choose one face as the top and fold its neighbours down around it. Their order around the top is fixed.
  4. A cube with the right faces in the wrong order around a corner (a mirror image) cannot be made.

concepts.title: Painted cube cut into n × n × n
concepts.body:
A cube painted on all faces is cut into n³ equal small cubes (n cuts along each edge give n pieces per edge).
Painted facesWhereCountn = 3n = 4n = 5
3Corners8888
2Edges, not corners12(n − 2)122436
1Middle of faces6(n − 2)²62454
0Hidden inside(n − 2)³1827

Check: the four counts add up to n³. Find n as the cube root of the number of pieces, or big side ÷ small side.

concepts.title: Painted cuboids and colours
concepts.body:
• Cuboid a × b × c cut into unit cubes: 3 faces = 8; 2 faces = 4[(a − 2) + (b − 2) + (c − 2)]; 1 face = 2[(a − 2)(b − 2) + (b − 2)(c − 2) + (c − 2)(a − 2)]; 0 faces = (a − 2)(b − 2)(c − 2).
  • The fewest colours needed so that no two adjacent faces share a colour is 3 (paint each opposite pair the same colour).

varieties.name: Opposite face from positions
varieties.how: Faces seen together are adjacent. With one common face, list each view clockwise from that face; matching positions are opposite.

example.q: Two positions of the same die are shown. Which number is on the face opposite 2?
steps: The common face is 1. It is on top in (i) and on the left in (ii).
Clockwise from 1 (top, right, left): view (i) gives 1, 3, 2 and view (ii) gives 1, 6, 5.
Matching positions are opposite: 3–6 and 2–5. The last pair is 1–4.

varieties.name: Opposite face in an open net
varieties.how: Skip one square along a straight line; in a Z or staircase, the end squares are opposite. Touching squares are never opposite.

example.q: The left-hand net in the figure is folded into a cube. Which number is opposite 2?
steps: 2 touches 1 and 3, so neither is opposite it.

varieties.name: Matching a net with a cube
varieties.how: Reject cubes that show an opposite pair. For the rest, fold one face as the top and check the order of its neighbours.

example.q: Which cube can be formed by folding the net?
steps: C, D, E lie in a row, so C and E are opposite (skip one). A, B, C, D form a staircase, so its ends A and D are opposite. That leaves B and F.
(a) shows C and E together, and (b) shows A and D together, so both are wrong.
Fold with C on top: B goes to the back, D to the right, F to the front, A to the left and E to the bottom.
Turn this cube half a turn: B comes to the front and A to the right, with C still on top. That is cube (d).
(c) has A and B swapped, a mirror image, so it cannot be made.

example.q: A cube painted on all faces is cut into 125 identical small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?

tips: Faces seen together in any view can never be opposite.
If one number appears in every view, the number never seen with it is its opposite.
In a net, skip one square along a line to find an opposite pair.
Check that your three opposite pairs use all six faces exactly once.
Corners of a painted cube are always 8, whatever the size.
The four painted-cube counts must add up to n³.
traps: Do not assume a standard die (opposites add to 7) unless the question says so.
A cube that shows only adjacent faces can still be impossible if the order around the corner is mirrored.
For a painted cube of side 6 cm cut into 2 cm cubes, n = 3, not 6.
Two views that share two faces still need the remaining faces checked one from each view.

questions.q: Two different positions of the same die are shown. Which number is on the face opposite to 1?
questions.solution:
In both views, 1 is on top.
Faces seen with 1: 2, 3 (view i) and 4, 5 (view ii).
So 2, 3, 4, 5 are adjacent to 1 and the remaining number 6 is opposite 1.

questions.q: The given sheet is folded to form a cube. Which number will be on the face opposite to 2?
questions.solution:
2, 3, 4 lie in one straight row. Skip one square: 2 and 4 are opposite.
(Other pairs: 1–5 and 3–6.)

questions.q: A cube painted on all its faces is cut into 64 identical small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
Three different positions of the same die are shown. Which number is on the face opposite to 4?
questions.solution:
View (ii): 4 is with 1 and 2.
View (iii): 4 is with 5 and 6.
So 1, 2, 5, 6 are adjacent to 4. The remaining number, 3, is opposite 4.
(Check: 3 never appears with 4 in any view.)

questions.q: The sheet shown in the figure is folded to form a cube. Which of the following cubes can be formed?
questions.solution:
Opposite pairs from the net: 1–5, 2–4, 3–6.
(a) shows 3 and 6 together ✗. (d) shows 1 and 5 together ✗.
(b) and (c) both show 2, 3, 5. Fold the net with 3 on top: 5 is in front, 4 on the right, 2 on the left, 1 at the back.
Turn the cube so 2 is on top (roll it to the right): 3 comes to the right face and 5 stays in front → top 2, front 5, right 3 = cube (b).
Cube (c) has 3 and 5 swapped, which is the mirror arrangement and cannot be made.

questions.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted red on all faces and then cut into small cubes of side 1 cm. How many small cubes have exactly one face painted?
